stem:
With reference to the Finance Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is a statutory body.
2. The Finance Commission was established under Article 280 of the Constitution.
3. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are only advisory in nature.
4. The first Finance Commission was established in
1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President at intervals of every five years, or earlier as required. Therefore, it is a constitutional body. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President. Its main function is to make recommendations to the President regarding the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, and the principles governing the allocation of such proceeds among the States. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory in nature. The Finance Commission also recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India. It submits its report to the President. It is noteworthy that the first Finance Commission was constituted on 22 November 1951 under the chairmanship of K. C. Neogy. The Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission is Arvind Panagariya.

stem: Who among the following determines the qualification which shall be requisite for appointment as member of the finance commission?
expl: Article 280(2) of the Constitution of India clearly provides that the required qualifications for the members of the Finance Commission and the manner of their selection may be determined by Parliament by making a law.

options.label: b
options.text: Allocate funds to various ministries of the Union and State Governments

options.label: c

expl: Article 280 of the Constitution provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President every five years or earlier, if necessary. The main function of the Finance Commission is to submit recommendations to the President regarding the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, and the allocation of the respective shares among the States.

stem: Who was the Chairman of the 12th Finance Commission?
expl: The 12th Finance Commission, constituted on 1 November 2002, was chaired by Dr. C. Rangarajan, former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. The recommendations of the 12th Finance Commission were for the period 2005–10. The 15th Finance Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of N. K. Singh on 27 November 2017. Its recommendations were originally to apply from 2020 to 2025; however, they were implemented in two phases, namely 2020–21 and 2021–26.

stem: Which of the following is nOT a member of the 15th Finance Commission?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The 15th Finance Commission was constituted on 27 November 2017 under the chairmanship of N. K. Singh. It had four members—Ajay Narayan Jha, Dr. Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Dr. Anoop Singh, and Professor Ramesh Chand. At the initial stage of the Commission’s formation, Shaktikanta Das was also a member, but later Ajay Narayan Jha was appointed as a member in his place. In December 2023, the 16th Finance Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of Dr. Arvind Panagariya. At present, the other four members of the 16th Finance Commission are as follows— 1. Annie George Mathew (full-time member) 2. Manoj Panda (full-time member) 3. Dr. Soumyakanti Ghosh (member) 4. T. Rabi Sankar (member) Earlier, Dr. Niranjan Rajadhyaksha was appointed as a full-time member, but in April 2024 he was replaced by Manoj Panda. Earlier, Ajay Narayan Jha, appointed as a full-time member, resigned from his post in April 2025 due to personal reasons.

stem: When was the Planning Commission established?
expl: The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, advisory and consultative body. It was not mentioned in the Constitution. It was constituted by a resolution of the Union Cabinet on 15 March 1950. The Prime Minister was its ex officio Chairperson. Its main function was to prepare the national Five-Year Plans and to determine the allocation of resources for the most effective and balanced use of the country’s resources. From 1 January 2015, it was replaced by the NITI Aayog. At present, the Chairperson of the NITI Aayog is Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Vice Chairperson is Suman Bery. The Prime Minister is the ex officio Chairperson of the NITI Aayog. NITI stands for “National Institution for Transforming India”.

expl: The special election held to fill a vacancy caused due to the death/resignation/disqualification, etc., of an elected member of the legislature is called a by-election.

stem: The lower age limit of voters of Union and State legislature was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by
expl: By the Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988, the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years, which came into force on 28 March 1989. Young voters first exercised the right to vote at the age of 18 in the general elections to the 9th Lok Sabha held in November 1989. The mention of “1989” in option (c) of the given question is incorrect; it should be “1988” instead.

stem: Who has the authority to grant national or regional party status to the various political parties in India?
expl: In India, the Election Commission has the authority to grant the status of a national or regional (state) party to political parties, for which it lays down certain criteria.

stem: What is the version of the machine vvPAT used for voting in India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: To supervise the prescribed election process and mechanism, the Constitution provides for the establishment of an independent body known as the Election Commission under Article 324. The use of Electronic Voting Machines has made the election system more transparent, simple, and convenient. For official verification of this transparency, the Election Commission uses the Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT). At present, the M3 version of the VVPAT machine is used by the Election Commission for voting. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
